chapter.heading: Man’s Wickedness and God’s PerfectionsTo the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David the servant of the Lord.
chapter.v:
An oracle
within my heart concerning the transgression of the wicked:There is no fear of God before his eyes. [Prov. 4:8, 9; Acts 6:15 b Deut.]

For he
flatters himself in his own eyes,When he finds out his iniquity and when he hates. [Ex. 22:11;]

The words
of his mouth are wickedness and deceit;He has ceased to be wise and to do good. [Eccl. 10:4]

He devises
wickedness on his bed;He sets himself in a way that is not good;He does not abhor evil. [1 Sam. 13:11, 13; Job 34:18]

Your mercy,
O Lord, is in the heavens;Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

Your righteousness
is like the great mountains;Your judgments are a great deep;O Lord, You preserve man and beast.

How precious
is Your lovingkindness, O God!Therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of Your wings. [Prov. 24:22; Eccl. 6:12]

They are
abundantly satisfied with the fullness of Your house,And You give them drink from the river of Your pleasures. [Ps. 49:6, 7; Job 14:5 i Deut. 20:5-8]

For with
You is the fountain of life;In Your light we see light.

Oh, continue
Your lovingkindness to those who know You,And Your righteousness to the upright in heart. [Eccl. 2:16; 9:5]

Let not
the foot of pride come against me,And let not the hand of the wicked drive me away. [Ps. 10:6; 50:21; Is. 26:10]

There the
workers of iniquity have fallen;They have been cast down and are not able to rise. [Is. 65:20; [Rom. 2:5-7] m [Deut. 4:40; Ps. 37:11, 18, 19; Prov. 1:32, 33; Is. 3:10; Matt. 25:34, 41]]
